reference_disclaimer: No image is being judged here and no asset changes either way. The decision is which property `verify_assets` asserts about the committed PNG bytes at `decode_png`. One correction matters more than anything else below, because a first version of this packet got it wrong: that term does NOT defend against a hand-edited sprite. Re-encoding edited pixels through the tool's own `encode_png` satisfies it today, and would satisfy a scanline comparison too. What catches an edited sprite is the provenance digest in `provenance.json`, which no option here touches. Every figure below was measured on this host by the script bound to this batch.

acceptance_criteria: The canon holds on an interpreter linked against either zlib or zlib-ng
It says which property it asserts, rather than implying pixel provenance it never had
The one-IDAT and empty-IEND properties byte equality provided are asserted explicitly rather than lost

audit_verdict.note: Measured directly. See the Measurement section on this subject.

subjects.description: Replace `data == encode_png(decode_png_bytes(data))` with explicit structural requirements: the existing chunk, format and size checks, plus the two properties byte equality was silently providing - exactly one IDAT, and an empty IEND payload. The compressed DEFLATE stream stops being asserted, which is what makes the canon hold on an interpreter linked against zlib-ng. This is the option the card favours; what has changed is the reason and the required additions.

items.definition: No. One channel changed and re-encoded through `encode_png` is accepted by the structural check, by today's byte-equality term, AND by a scanline comparison. This corrects the first version of this packet, which reported a rejection by comparing against the committed asset - a reference `decode_png` does not have, since it runs on source files with no expected image.
items.term: Does the canon term stop a hand-edited sprite?

items.definition: The provenance digest. `provenance.json` records sha256 3a52a8b1... for the master; the altered file hashes af2357e0..., and `_validate_provenance` raises `provenance source digest mismatch` (scripts/dif_assets.py:612-620). No option in this decision touches that.

A level-6 recompression with identical pixels and filters (the zlib-ng case); a non-empty IEND payload; and an IDAT split in two. All three are accepted by the structural check and have identical decoded scanlines, so byte equality is the only thing rejecting them - and two of the three have nothing to do with which zlib is installed.
items.term: What byte equality actually adds - three things, not one

items.definition: One IDAT chunk, canon term holds, 745,543 bytes.

subjects.display_name: Option 1 - assert canonical structure explicitly and stop comparing compressed bytes

identity_files.label: The measurement output on this host

known_concerns: Written naively as a scanline comparison it would be vacuous: `_filtered_rgba_rows` emits filter byte 0 for every row, so the comparison can only ever agree. The value is in the explicit structural requirements, not in comparing scanlines.

It stops pinning the exact serialization. A future generator change that altered compression would no longer be caught here - only by the provenance digests, and only for files whose digests are re-recorded.
The measurement was taken on a host whose interpreter links stock zlib 1.2.12, where the canon currently passes. The failure it addresses was observed elsewhere.

acceptance_criteria: Byte equality survives an interpreter change
The added dependency or the second copy of every compressed stream is an accepted cost

audit_verdict.note: Not implemented. Selecting this makes it the implementation.

subjects.description: Keep asserting the exact compressed bytes, and make them reproducible by vendoring a deterministic DEFLATE implementation or by storing each asset's expected IDAT stream alongside it. This is the only option that keeps the serialization pinned exactly.
subjects.display_name: Option 2 - keep byte equality and pin the compressor

identity_files.label: The measurement output on this host

known_concerns: A vendored DEFLATE is a new build-time dependency in a tool that currently has none beyond the standard library.
Storing expected IDAT streams doubles the compressed bytes in the repository for every asset and adds a second thing that can drift.

It keeps a property whose demonstrated effects are a recompression that changes no pixel, a non-empty IEND payload, and IDAT splitting - none of which is the hand-edited sprite the canon was thought to be defending against.

acceptance_criteria: Accepted only as a deliberate decision that the next host rediscovers this

audit_verdict.note: Recorded so the choice is complete. The card rejects it: it fixes this host and breaks the next, and it is the only option that rewrites committed asset bytes.

subjects.description: Leave the canon alone and re-encode every committed asset so byte equality holds against whichever zlib produced them most recently.
